1429.13: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Raagmala. With each raag go five consorts (raginis), and (the singers) intone its eight sons along with them. First they (the singers) perform Raag Bhairao, and with it they voice five raginis: first Bhairavi (and) Bilavali; (then) they sing Punniaki and Bangli; then came the turn of Asalekhi. These are the five wives of Bhairao. They let Pancham, Harakh and Disakh be heard, and sing Bangalam, Madhu and Madhav; Lalat and Bilaval (too) they sing, each in its own manner: the singers sing (these) eight sons of Bhairav. Second, they intone Malkausak, (and) set five raginis with it: Gondkari and Devgandhari, Gandhari (and) Sihuti were voiced, (and) Dhanasari: these five were sung, joined with Raag Malkausak. Maru, Mastang, Mevara, Prabalchand, Kausak, Ubhara, Khaukhat and Bhauranad were sung: these eight (sons) are joined with Malkausak. Then came Hindol, with five wives and eight sons; taans (runs of notes) rise in play, and the singers tune the strings. Telangi (and) Devkari came, Basanti (and) Sandur, graceful; taking Ahiri, full of charm, as a wife, (Hindol) has joined all five consorts to himself. Surmanand (and) Bhaskar came, Chandrabimb (and) Manglan, graceful; Sarasban and Binoda are (there); (and) sweetly they sing Basant (and) Kamoda. I have named (these) eight sons, set out with care; then came the turn of Deepak. Kacheli, Patmanjari (and) Todi were intoned and sung; Kamodi and Gujri were set with Deepak. Kalanka, Kuntal and Rama, those named Kamalkusam (and) Champak, Gaura, Kanra and Kalyana: know these as the eight sons of Deepak. All together they sing Sri Raag, (and) set five consorts with it: Bairari (and) Karnati were placed, they sing Gavri (and) Asavari; after them Sindhvi was intoned: (these) five were set with Sri Raag. Salu, Sarag, Sagara, and Gond, Gambhir, Gund, Kumbh (and) Hamir: (these are) the eight sons of Sri Raag. Sixth, they sing Megh Raag, (and) set five consorts with it: Sorath, Gond, the melody of Malari; then the skilled sing the graces of Asa; then, in a high note, Suhau was sung: (these) five are known as Megh Raag's. Bairadhar, Gajdhar, Kedara, Jablidhar, Nat and Jaldhara, then they sing Sankar and Siama: these are the names of Megh Raag's sons. They have sung six raags, with thirty raginis, and all the sons of the raags, eighteen, ten and twenty (forty-eight). ॥1॥
